los.text: Describe the clinical features of diabetic ketoacidosis and explain how these relate to the underlying pathophysiology and management.
Describe the key investigations used in the diagnosis and monitoring of type 1 diabetes and diabetic ketoacidosis.
Explain the pathophysiology of type 1 diabetes and how this relates to its clinical presentation, diagnosis, and long-term management.
Link the key functional and morphological features of type I diabetes to its clinical signs and symptoms.
Describe how the system in Wales works with regards to the assessment of new drugs and the process to decide their availability (or not) for prescribing.
sessions: Resource Allocation in a Pharmacy context

los.text: Describe the principles of management of type 1 diabetes, including acute and long-term treatment strategies.
Apply the pharmacology of insulin and relevant evidence to be able to choose and manage effective treatment for individual patients
Interpret clinical data sets (e.g. blood results, ECGs, imaging, observations) within a gamified, interactive format, applying clinical reasoning to select appropriate responses
Demonstrate structured wrist and hand examination, hip examination, knee examination and foot and ankle examinations.
Analyse clinical findings in the context of anatomical knowledge to identify potential underlying pathologies affecting the wrist and hand, hip, knee or foot and ankle.
Formulate an appropriate plan for further investigation or referral, based on clinical findings and current guidelines.
Clearly and concisely present clinical findings from a musculoskeletal examination using appropriate medical terminology and structure.
Predict the effects of pathology on the anatomy of the gastrointestinal tract
los.html:
PathologyAnatomical basisEffects you can predict
Oesophageal cancerLower third (adenocarcinoma, Barrett's) or middle (squamous); three narrowings
  • Progressive dysphagia (solids then liquids)
  • Spread to the left recurrent laryngeal nerve (hoarse), trachea (fistula)
  • Lymph to mediastinal and coeliac nodes
Hiatus herniaStomach through the oesophageal hiatus (T10); crura weakReflux (lost sphincter angle), rolling type can strangulate
Peptic ulcerPosterior duodenal ulcer next to the gastroduodenal artery; anterior ulcer faces the peritoneal cavityPosterior: massive bleeding; anterior: perforation → air under the diaphragm, peritonitis, shoulder-tip pain
Gastric cancerLymph via the thoracic ductVirchow's node (left supraclavicular), Sister Mary Joseph nodule (umbilicus), Krukenberg (ovaries)
Pancreatic head cancerCBD passes through the headPainless obstructive jaundice, palpable gallbladder (Courvoisier), duodenal obstruction
GallstonesHartmann's pouch, cystic duct, CBD, ampullaColic, cholecystitis (Murphy's sign), obstructive jaundice, gallstone pancreatitis, gallstone ileus (fistula to duodenum, stuck at the ileocaecal valve)
AppendicitisMidgut visceral pain (T10) then parietal peritoneum (somatic)Periumbilical pain shifting to the RIF; retrocaecal → psoas sign; pelvic → urinary and rectal symptoms
Small bowel obstruction (adhesions, hernias)Narrow points: hernial necks (femoral below and lateral to the pubic tubercle)Colicky pain, vomiting, distension; dilated loops with valvulae conniventes across the whole width
Large bowel obstruction (cancer, volvulus)Sigmoid on a long mesentery; competent ileocaecal valveClosed loop: caecum dilates most and may perforate (>9–12 cm); haustra don't cross the full width; "coffee-bean" sigmoid volvulus
Colorectal cancerWatershed and lymph follow arteriesRight: anaemia, mass; left: change in bowel habit, obstruction; rectal: bleeding, tenesmus; liver metastases via the portal vein
Diverticular diseaseMucosa herniates where vessels pierce the sigmoid wall (no complete longitudinal muscle: taeniae)LIF pain, bleeding, abscess, fistula (bladder: pneumaturia)
Ischaemic colitisWatershed areas: splenic flexure (Griffiths' point) and rectosigmoid (Sudeck's point)Pain and bloody diarrhoea in older vascular patients
Portal hypertensionPortosystemic anastomosesOesophageal varices, caput medusae, rectal varices, splenomegaly, ascites
HaemorrhoidsAnal cushions above the pectinate line (visceral nerves)Painless bright red bleeding; perianal haematoma below the line is painful
Anal fissure / perianal abscessBelow the pectinate line (somatic, pudendal); ischioanal fossaVery painful; abscesses track to the ischioanal fossa, horseshoe round the back
